summary.text: Scott Soracco is the Democratic candidate for the Georgia House of Representatives, District 29, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Republican Matt Dubnik.
A retired Army officer and former federal emergency management operations officer, he says his policy interests include healthcare, mental health, veterans issues and education.

paragraphs.text: Soracco served in the U.S. Army from 1984 to 2012.

He earned a high school diploma from Woodward Academy, a bachelor's degree from North Georgia College in 1984 and a graduate degree from the Army War College in 2011, and Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working as an operations director.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he has lived in the Gainesville and Oakwood area since 1968 and described himself as a retired Army officer with combat and senior staff experience who recently retired as a federal emergency manager operations officer, and who worked for ten years as a financial consultant and registered representative.
Soracco said in the survey that government should reflect citizens' values and that he wants to expand access to affordable healthcare and protect freedom of choice on reproductive rights.
He listed healthcare, mental health, veterans issues, education, environmental stewardship and citizen voting access as his state-level policy interests.
